## Topic & main goal

```{=html}
<div class="slide-inner">
  <h2 class="slide-heading"><span class="slide-num">01</span> Topic &amp; main goal</h2>
  <ul class="goal-list">
    <li>Explore the relationship between measurable audio features and track popularity</li>
    <li>Compare how audio profiles differ across music genres</li>
    <li>Identify what a “popular” song sounds like, and how that varies by genre</li>
  </ul>
  <div class="central-q"><strong>Central question:</strong> What makes a Spotify track popular?</div>
  <div class="pull-quote" style="margin-top:0.65em"><p><strong>Main goal:</strong> Help music fans explore patterns in Spotify audio data: clearly, interactively, and without a hit formula.</p></div>
</div>
```

```{=html}

</div>
```

## Key insights

```{=html}
<div class="slide-inner">
  <h2 class="slide-heading"><span class="slide-num">09</span> Key insights</h2>
  <p class="slide-note" style="margin:0 0 0.75em">Headlines only. Charts &amp; interaction in the <strong>live demo</strong> next</p>
  <ul class="insights-list">
    <li><strong>Most songs are never heard</strong><span class="insight-detail">Only 3.5% score above 70; 10.5% sit at zero.</span></li>
    <li><strong>Audio features don’t predict popularity well</strong><span class="insight-detail">Correlations are weak (strongest: instrumentalness, r ≈ −0.13).</span></li>
    <li><strong>Genres have very different profiles</strong><span class="insight-detail">No single “sound” for all music.</span></li>
    <li><strong>Hits vs. non-hits overlap heavily</strong><span class="insight-detail">Patterns describe differences, not a recipe for success.</span></li>
  </ul>
  <div class="pull-quote" style="margin-top:0.85em"><p>We show the evidence in the story, not on this slide.</p></div>

</div>
```
